creator: malcolm_alexanderr
caption:
Great for meal prep or even for events like game day!

ingredients:
* 1 1/b lbs 93% lean ground beef 
* 12oz box protein wheat pasta
* 1/2 cup blended low fat cottage cheese 
* 1 container of mushrooms 
* 15oz jar tomato sauce 
* 2 tbsp ketchup 
* 1 tbsp Dijon or yellow mustard 
* 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce 
* 1 tbsp dill pickle juice 
* 1 cup nonfat milk
* 1 1/2 cups low sodium beef broth 
* 1/2 cup shredded cheddar cheese 

#mealprep #crockpotrecipes #healthymealideas #budget #budgeting

transcript.text: I'm a 29 year old teacher who grocery shops on a $50 weekly budget.
Let me show you what I meal prep using what I buy.
Today in the crock pot, I'm going to be making a healthy protein pack cheeseburger pasta.
With 475 calories and 40 grams of protein per serving, you're not even going to need to
go to the drive-thru.
So let me show you how to make it.
First up, about 1 and a half pounds of ground beef in your crock pot.
I ground my ground beef on the stove and I also bought the 93% lean ground beef.
Season with some salt, pepper, onion powder,
Kinder's garlic butter, but you can add garlic powder if you don't have this.
Paprika and some of the sugar-free barbecue rub.
Next, I'm going to add in some chopped mushrooms.
Please make sure you clean your mushrooms before you put them in the crock pot.
They literally come from the ground.
A 15 ounce jar of tomato sauce,
2 tablespoons of sugar-free ketchup,
1 tablespoon of mustard,
1 tablespoon of Worcestershire sauce,
1 tablespoon of dill pickle juice,
1 cup of non-fat milk,
and 1 and a half cups of low sodium beef broth.
Now I'm going to give everything in my crock pot a good mix.
My lid is on, I'm going to cook this on low for about four hours
and I'm going to clean my apartment in the meantime.
I'm not going to film this part,
but I'm going to cook this entire 12 ounce box of Banza Wheat Protein Pasta.
And while my pasta cooks,
I'm going to put in about half a cup of cottage cheese, low-fat cottage cheese.
Everything in my crock pot is done cooking,
so now I'm going to add in my protein pasta,
my cottage cheese mix,
and half a cup of shredded cheddar cheese.
Now I'm going to mix everything in my crock pot until my cheese is fully melted.
And just like that, I have now made four servings of this healthy hamburger pasta
with each serving measuring at about one and a half cups.
As always, thank you for watching.
I love you guys so much and I'll see you next time.

hook.template: I'm a [AGE] year old [JOB] who [MONEY OR TIME LIMIT]. Let me show you what I make
hook.whyItWorks: Age, job and a dollar figure in one sentence make it instantly real and specific. A tight budget is a challenge viewers want to see solved, and the on-screen bubble repeats it for anyone watching muted.

format.visualLayout: One locked-off wide shot: creator behind a slow cooker on a kitchen island, talking to camera while adding ingredients, sticker-style text bubbles
format.pacing: steady, jump cuts about every 2 to 3s in one fixed frame, with one outfit-change time skip at about 61s
format.reasoning: A single fixed frame makes it feel like a friend cooking with you, and a slow cooker lets every step be 'add this, add that' with no technique to film. Calories and protein on screen early give fitness viewers the reason to stay for the full 94s.

myVersion.script:
I coach women on fat loss and my weekly grocery budget is ₹[YOUR BUDGET]. Here's what four lunches look like.
One pressure cooker. One big batch. Soya chunk and rajma pulao.
Why soya? It's one of the cheapest protein sources in any kirana store.
First, soak a cup of soya chunks in hot water for ten minutes. Squeeze out the water. This part matters, or they stay rubbery.
Rajma I soaked last night. If you forgot, use a tin, no judgement.
Cooker on. A spoon of oil, jeera, one big onion, sliced thin.
Let the onion go golden. Don't rush this. That's where the flavour comes from.
Ginger garlic paste. Two chopped tomatoes. Haldi, red chilli, garam masala, salt.
Cook it till the oil separates.
Now the soya chunks and the rajma go in. Mix so every piece is coated.
Add rice. I'm using a cup and a half. Brown rice if you have it, regular is fine too.
Water, about double the rice. Two whistles. Switch off and let the pressure drop on its own.
While that happens, I chop cucumber, onion and tomato for kachumber and whisk some curd with salt and roasted jeera.
Open the cooker. Fluff it gently with a fork so the rice doesn't break and the soya stays whole.
Four boxes. Pulao, salad on the side, a little raita.
Every box has protein from two sources, fibre, and a carb that keeps you full till evening.
Look at the protein on your soya pack and you'll see why I keep buying it.
Total cost for all four lunches? About ₹[YOUR COST]. Less than one restaurant thali.
You don't need fancy powders or imported stuff to eat high protein. You need a cooker, a plan and one free hour on Sunday.
